notes: Checked main header nav (single top-level nav item whose LINK TEXT is literally 'New Arrivals' -> /collection/fall-collection-26), footer, and sitemap/collections.sitemap.xml (grepped for new/arriv/just/latest/recent), which surfaced a second, nav-orphaned candidate /collection/new--now ('New & Now'). Both pages are genuine cross-category product grids (real filters e.g. Bedroom Furniture / Candlelight & Home Fragrance / Bath Linens, sortOn=popular, cursor pagination) confirmed via each page's own embedded product-listing JSON, i.e. real PLPs and not lookbook/marketing pages. However neither is unambiguous: (1) /collection/fall-collection-26 is the page the site's own 'New Arrivals' nav link currently points to, but the PAGE'S OWN title/og:title is 'Fall Collection 26 | Explore Fall Collection', a themed seasonal-campaign-style name, not literally 'New Arrivals' -- per the brief's Collection-page rule this is flagged rather than assumed. (2) /collection/new--now ('New & Now', a standard new-arrivals-style name) is NOT linked from the main nav or footer at all -- it is only discoverable via the sitemap -- raising the question of whether it is a stale/superseded page or a legitimate supplementary New Arrivals hub; it reports a much larger item_total (136) than the nav-designated page (24), and could not be confirmed as an alias of fall-collection-26 (very different counts, so treated as a genuinely different listing per the multiple-PLPs rule, not deduplicated). Both are recorded as separate rows with MANUAL REVIEW flags rather than a unilateral include/exclude call. No further New-Arrivals-type candidates (Just In / Latest / Recently Added / What's New) were found anywhere in nav, footer, or the collections sitemap. Access: direct HTTP GET throughout, no WAF/block; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow and does not block singular /collection/... paths used here (only /collections* plural).
